title: Exceptional-adjoint admissibility datum
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
$p,a_0,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and the finite coefficient conventions
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes
and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the bounded constructible finite-Tor
categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the
compact-support direct image of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
and the constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

Say that $f$ is *exceptionally admissible at $A$* when the restrictions
$$
 Rf_!:D^b_{ctf}(X,A)\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(Y,A),\qquad
 Rf^!:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(X,A)
$$
are equipped with the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, with natural unit
$\eta_f:\operatorname{id}\to Rf^!Rf_!$ and counit
$\varepsilon_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to\operatorname{id}$ satisfying both triangle
identities, and with the composition and base-change exchange
isomorphisms used in the trace-formula constructions. Here $Rf^!$ is the
specified constructible functor, rather than an unspecified ambient right adjoint.
The composition comparison is the conjugate
[def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of compact-support composition
[thm-sf-comp-composition], using the composite adjunction
[def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]: for a finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ and composable separated finite-type
$k$-morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$, it identifies
$R(hf)^!\cong Rf^!Rh^!$.

For base change, in a Cartesian square with top arrow $g':X'\to X$,
bottom arrow $g:Y'\to Y$, and vertical arrows $f',f$, all separated of
finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, the exchange meant here is
the conjugate under the composite adjunctions
$$
 Lg^*Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg_*,\qquad
 Rf'_!Lg'^*\dashv Rg'_*Rf'^!
$$
of the compact-support exchange
$Lg^*Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*$ of
[thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Thus its type is
$$Rg'_*Rf'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg_*.$$
The pullbacks and ordinary direct images here are those of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image].
The ordinary adjunction $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ (and likewise for $g'$) is the derived module adjunction of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Their finite-Tor constructible restrictions are supplied by
[lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale].

Say that $f$ is *exceptionally admissible* when this holds at every finite
coefficient stage $A_{E,n}$, with uniform bounds independent of $n$.
Here uniform bounds mean fixed signed integers $c_f^-,c_f^+$ such that a
constructible cohomological interval $[a,b]$
[def-weil-constructible-intervals] is carried by $Rf^!$ into
$[a+c_f^-,b+c_f^+]$, and the same assertion holds for a Tor interval
$[a,b]$ on a finite-Tor constructible input.

The availability of this datum is a theorem for every $f$ above, not an
additional hypothesis on the morphism. The adjunction and refinement
compatibility are [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], restricted to the full
finite-Tor constructible categories; the construction and uniform
preservation assertion for arbitrary finite-type $Y$ are stated in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For separated $Y$, the explicit
stage-independent bounds are also summarized in
[thm-sf-preservation-class]. The compact-support restriction is obtained
by $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$ from
[lem-trf-open-ctf, cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]; the composition and
base-change identifications above are the conjugates of those of $Rf_!$.
The trace-formula chapter names the datum only to specify the functor and
its adjunction maps. No strong ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is assumed, and no preservation
clause is an assumption: the ambient $\operatorname{FullCD}$ datum on every
pro-etale sheaf fails in general, for example for an elliptic curve over
$\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with coefficients $\mathbf F_r$, $r\ne p$, as
recorded in that definition.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. Say that $f$ is
*exceptionally admissible at $A$* when the compact-support direct image
$Rf_!:D^b_{ctf}(X,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has a specified right adjoint
$Rf^!:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with unit
$\operatorname{id}\to Rf^!Rf_!$ and counit
$Rf_!Rf^!\to\operatorname{id}$ (i.e. the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$),
and the composition and base-change exchange isomorphisms used below; and
*exceptionally admissible* when this holds at every finite coefficient stage
$A=A_{E,n}$ with constants independent of $n$. The functor in question is
the constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The condition is a *theorem*, not a restriction: every separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes is exceptionally admissible, the
adjunction on $D^b_{ctf}$, the preservation
$Rf^!D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\subseteq D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with stage-independent constants,
and the composition and base-change isomorphisms (the mates of those of
$Rf_!$) all holding for the constructible exceptional inverse image. Nothing
of the strong ambient notion of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]
— the ambient datum $\operatorname{FullCD}$ on every pro-etale sheaf together
with an ambient right adjoint — is assumed: that datum fails in general (for
an elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$).

lean.note: Finite-stage adjunction data on the canonical fixed-scalar presentation of the recorded intrinsic finite-Tor category; the exceptional functor is sfFiniteExceptionalAt. Composition and base-change comparisons are explicit conjugateIsoEquiv constructions from the specified left comparisons. Positive stages are indexed by n+1. The public predicates obtain compactifiability from the existing theorem, with no added geometric hypothesis.
